result.summary: Adds 0-of-0 OP_CHECKMULTISIG and OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY test cases for tapscript in feature_taproot.py to verify that failure is triggered specifically by the opcode ban rather than DER signature validation errors. Also dumps the expected error string for failure cases into the test assets and verifies in script_assets_tests that evaluation fails with the exact expected script error code under the declared flags.
result.problem: Existing tapscript test cases for disabled CHECKMULTISIG opcodes supplied Schnorr signatures, which fail DER signature validation when the opcode is executed. As a result, an implementation that incorrectly executes CHECKMULTISIG in tapscript still passed all tests. Additionally, the script asset test runner only verified that a test failed, without ensuring it failed for the correct reason.
evidence: The author found this flaw against external software: "This came up while running script_assets_test.json against a third-party implementation which executed OP_CHECKMULTISIG in tapscript and passed every case... it accepts the new failure case while its fixed version rejects it with SCRIPT_ERR_TAPSCRIPT_CHECKMULTISIG" (PR description).
result.card: Adds 0-of-0 OP_CHECKMULTISIG and OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY test vectors for tapscript to feature_taproot.py, and records expected error strings in the generated test asset dump for script_assets_tests to verify. Existing test cases used Schnorr signatures that failed DER validation, allowing an implementation that failed to disable CHECKMULTISIG in tapscript to pass all existing asset tests. The asset test runner also previously only verified that negative test cases failed, rather than verifying they failed with the expected error code. The author identified the issue after discovering a third-party tapscript implementation executing CHECKMULTISIG passed the test suite.

risk.why: Changes are strictly confined to functional test script generation and test harness assertions.
